documents.title: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.4 Application for licensure (procedure manual submission and program description)
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Human Services, Office of Licensing / Division of Developmental Disabilities
documents.how_used: Gives the submission sequence. After the application is approved and before a residence opens, the applicant submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing. After the manual is approved, the applicant submits job descriptions to DDD.

required_items.text: The licensee shall develop and implement a manual of written procedures to ensure that the service delivery system complies with State law and rules governing community residences for individuals with developmental disabilities.
The procedures shall be reviewed annually and revised as necessary.

Each procedure shall be designed in accordance with the principles of normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction, person centered planning and shall be consistent with the organizational structure and management philosophy of the licensee.
A descriptive title which is unique so as to permit easy reference and retrieval of each document;
An explanation regarding the purpose of the document;
A description of sequential steps required to successfully complete a task or action;
Assignment of staff responsibilities at each step in the implementation; and
Reporting and recording requirements for each person involved.
A statement of philosophy, values and goals so as to govern the organization's direction and character;
A table of organization that illustrates lines of authority, responsibility and communication;
A procedure for assuring compliance with the Central Registry;
A New Employee Orientation Checklist, which shall include, at a minimum, all requirements at N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.6(a)1 through 8;
The organization's philosophy, goals, services and practices;
The prevention of abuse, neglect and exploitation;
Unusual incident reporting and investigating procedures;

Emergency procedures as identified in the procedure manual; for example, the emergency evacuation plan, emergency medical treatment, emergency coverage and on-call procedures, the operation of the fire alarm system, and use of fire extinguishers;
An overview of developmental disabilities and any special needs of the individuals being served, for example, medical or behavioral problems requiring specific, tailored training;
The appropriate job description and the personnel policies of the organization, including its drug testing policies;
Training in life-threatening emergencies through a curriculum developed by the Division; and
Training consistent with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6.
A procedure for implementing a plan to deal with major emergencies requiring evacuation from the residence, such as a fire or a gas leak.

The procedure shall also address emergencies where evacuation may not be required, such as when the indoor air temperature is below 68 degrees Fahrenheit or above 82 degrees Fahrenheit for four consecutive hours;

A procedure for handling medical emergencies that includes the requirement to call 9-1-1 in the event of a life-threatening emergency, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-5.1 et seq. (Danielle's Law), and N.J.A.C. 10:42A;
Emergency coverage and on-call procedures;
A procedure for reporting all unusual incidents, including, but not limited to:
A written statement expressly prohibiting abuse, neglect, or exploitation; and
A written statement regarding the obligation to report each allegation as required at N.J.S.A. 9:68.10 and N.J.S.A. 52:27G-1 et seq., and Department policy.
required_items.cite: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)8.ii (statute citation printed as in the source text)

required_items.text: A procedure for investigations;
A procedure to ensure sound fiscal management of individual's personal funds;
A procedure for the safekeeping of valuable personal possessions;
A list and schedule of all charges and fees for which an individual shall be held responsible;

A procedure for resolving complaints and grievances of individuals that has a minimum of two levels at which the grievance shall be heard, the last of which involves the licensee or the executive director;
A procedure, separate from individuals' records, for internal communication, to include the use of a separate log to document critical information and the action taken by the licensee to follow-up:
Each log entry shall be dated and signed with the full name of the staff person making the entry;
A procedure for admissions that complies with the requirements at N.J.A.C. 10:44A-4;
A statement regarding maintaining confidentiality of individuals receiving services and records, as required at N.J.A.C. 10:41-2;
Written procedures for medication administration, including procedures for self-medication;
Written procedures for assuring compliance with the requirements for testing employees for controlled dangerous substances, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5;

Written procedures for the exchange of contact information of parents, family members who are actively involved in ensuring the individual's welfare, or guardians who choose to, as set forth at N.J.S.A. 30:6D-9.5 and 9.6;
A procedure for assuring that no employee is included on the Department of Children and Families' Child Abuse Registry, as set forth at N.J.S.A. 30:6D-73 et seq., and 9:6-8.10f;
A procedure to address the use of video/audio monitoring in the common areas of the residences, if applicable; and
A continuous quality improvement system to identify opportunities to improve services and/or supports and to resolve identified problems. The system shall include, at a minimum:
A written plan to identify how data is collected, analyzed, and utilized to determine patterns that identify process or systemic problems requiring further in-depth review;
Input from a variety of sources, including persons receiving services, family members, and others;
A written summary of satisfaction surveys;
A written summary of outcomes assessments; and
An action plan based upon an analysis at (b)22i through iv above.

Upon approval of the manual, the applicant shall submit job descriptions to the Division of Developmental Disabilities for each position included on the table of organization in the procedure manual, for review and approval.

"Program description" means a document submitted to obtain a license from the Department. A program description includes a description of services provided to individuals and staff coverage that assures supervision to every individual served at the program, in accordance with their service plan, and is reviewed as part of the licensing inspection process. The program description is amended, as necessary.
required_items.cite: N.J.A.C. 10:44A-1.3 (definition, quoted from the 2/5/2024 version of the chapter PDF)

sections: 2.2(a) General requirements for every procedure (annual review; normalization, age appropriateness, least restriction, person-centered planning; required elements i-v)
2.2(b)1-22 Documents and procedures to be in the procedure manual, in the regulation's own numbered order
2.6(a)1-8 New Employee Orientation Checklist content (required by 2.2(b)4)

notes: No official Office of Licensing policy checklist form was found. The regulation itself is the review standard. N.J.A.C. 10:44A-2.2(b)1-22 is the enumerated list of required manual contents. Sequence under 10:44A-1.4: (1) The applicant starts with the DDD Combined Application to Become a Medicaid/DDD Approved Provider and the Attestation for Individual Supports Provider. (2) The application must be complete within 45 days. The Department decides within 60 days. (3) After approval and before opening a residence, the applicant submits the procedure manual to the Office of Licensing, which approves it if it meets 10:44A-2.2. Licensees already operating residences with approved manuals are exempt. (4) After manual approval, the applicant submits job descriptions for every position on the table of organization to DDD for review and approval. Organize the manual in the numbered order of 2.2(b)1-22 so a reviewer can map each procedure to a citation. Each procedure should have a unique descriptive title, a purpose statement, sequential steps, staff responsibilities at each step, and reporting and recording requirements (2.2(a)3.i-v). Review the manual annually. Other subchapters (3 rights, 4 admission and service plans, 5 health and safety including medication, 6 fire safety and evacuation) set content that the procedures must follow. They are cross-referenced by 2.2(b)15 and 2.2(b)17, but I did not list them item by item because 2.2(b) is the enumerated list. The 1.4(c)1 application contents (table of organization, curricula vitae, owner and financial documents and similar) are application paperwork and are excluded, apart from the program description and the table of organization, which also appears in 2.2(b)2. The readoption notice (58 N.J.R. 1193(b)) says further rulemaking may be needed, so check the Office of Licensing site for later amendments.
